summary: The top of a profile page: the person's avatar and name, a one-line subtitle (role or team), optional meta such as availability, and one or two actions.
whenToUse: Once at the top of a page about one person: a profile, a team member page, an account page.
subtitle: the role and team, the way colleagues would describe the person.
meta: one or two facts that help someone decide to reach out, like availability or local time.
actions: what you can do with this person (Message) or with your own profile (Edit profile).
whenNotToUse: Lists of people: use Avatar with the name in a table or list row.
Pages about a thing, not a person: use PageHeader.
The signed-in user menu: use Avatar in the top bar.

dos.title: Write the name as the person wrote it
dos.text: Keep accents, hyphens and capitals. The header wraps long names instead of cutting them.

donts.title: Pack the subtitle
donts.text: One line about the role. Contact details and bios belong in the page content.

p.name: Dana Moreau
p.subtitle: Product designer, Payments, Paris office, dana@example.com, joined in 2021, mentor

accessibility: Renders a header with a real heading for the name (h1 by default), so the page outline starts with the person.
The avatar is decorative here: the heading already says the name, so screen readers do not hear it twice.
Actions keep their own roles: a Button for actions, a link for navigation.
contentGuidelines: Name: as the person wrote it, never truncated.
Subtitle: role and team, sentence case, no trailing period.
